note: Known, pre-existing typography debt, PER FILE. Written by
`node tools/type-linkage/check.mjs --update-baseline`.
Each entry is a typographic value that does not resolve through --sa-type-*.
`size-off-ramp` is the worse half: a size the 21-role scale cannot express at
all (13px appears 71 times), so it needs a DESIGN decision — snap to 12 or 14 —
not merely a binding. The rest are values that happen to match the scale and
are one edit from being bound.
The decision (2026-09-01) is to clear these as pages are redesigned, rather
than sweep now: snapping 13px moves text on live government pages and every
one needs a visual audit first.
This file is a RATCHET, not a permission slip. The gate fails if a count GROWS
or a new file appears, and fails if a count SHRINKS without this file being
updated — so the backlog can only go down. Re-run --update-baseline in the
same change that clears some.
RECORDED AGAINST THE COMMITTED TREE, not the working one. An earlier version was
written from a dirty checkout and froze PageHero.tsx at counts that did not exist on
main, so the gate failed the moment it ran anywhere else. A baseline is a claim about
the branch; generate it from what the branch actually contains.
Re-recorded after merging origin/main. Fifty-two commits landed while this branch was
open and brought their own typography with them — site-page-header.css, fact-strip.css,
two Storybook stories and a chart leading. Those are INHERITED debt, not new violations:
the ratchet's contract is that the change which brings a file in re-baselines it, in the
same commit, so the number can still only go down from here.
First clearing (2026-09-01): site-page-header.css went 2 leadings to 0. Both were
RATIOS, not literals a sweep would obviously catch — `1.2` on the title and `1.5` on
the standfirst. Each was exact at precisely one viewport and one surface and wrong at
every other, which is why they read as correct for so long. A ratio beside a bound
size is the failure mode this gate exists for.
